paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole chapter is shouting: God's grace is a gift, and you can't buy it, earn it or bargain for it. Naaman showed up with silver, gold, ten sets of clothing, horses and chariots, and the cure came in one simple instruction: "Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan" (2 Kings 5:10). He almost missed it because it looked too small and too plain. Pride will tell you the way God heals has to be fancy, and Naaman's servants had to remind him that it didn't (2 Kings 5:13).

Look at what happened once Naaman obeyed. His flesh was "restored and became like that of a little child," and he said, "Now I know for sure that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel" (2 Kings 5:14-15). Notice who started the whole thing, too: a young girl taken from her home, who still spoke up about the prophet (2 Kings 5:2-3). I think God can use the smallest voice in the room, and your obedience may be bigger than you know. So when His word sounds too simple, DO IT anyway, because the humble thing is usually the healing thing.

Then comes Gehazi, and he's the warning. Elisha said no to the gift, and Gehazi ran down the road to grab what grace had given away for free. He lied to Naaman, then lied to Elisha, and he walked out carrying the very leprosy Naaman left behind (2 Kings 5:27). Friend, I got picked out of a bargain bin for a quarter, and I know I never earned a thing. Keep your hands open to receive what God gives, and don't go chasing what you think you can get out of it.
